newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries virtually flat by Tokyo noon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries virtually flat by Tokyo noon.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were little changed in quiet trade by Tokyo midday on Wednesday, but the market's tone was firm following overnight gains, traders said.
Solid bids were detected in five- and ten-year notes, traders said.
The 6-1/4 percent 5-year note stood at 100-13/32, yielding 6.15 percent, compared with 100-12/32 in New York on late Tuesday.
The 6-5/8 percent 10-year note was at 102-23/32, yielding 6.25 percent, compared with Tuesday's New York close of 102-22/32.
Traders said they were watching whether the dollar's sharp overnight rise versus the yen would prompt Japanese investors to take profits. So far, such selling has not been detected, they said.
The dollar was trading at around 115.30/35 yen at 0310 GMT, after jumping above 115 yen overnight.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 101-02/32, yielding 6.54 percent, versus Tuesday's New York close of 101-01/32.
Traders said the U.S. consumer price index (CPI) for June due at 1230 GMT is widely expected to confirm stable prices and be market-supportive.
A Reuters poll sees a rise of 0.2 percent for both the CPI and core CPI versus gains of 0.1 percent and 0.2 percent for each in May.
"The market sees little risk of inflation in the United States. So a CPI figure slightly higher than expected, say 0.3 percent, is unlikely to trigger selling," said a trader at a Japanese bank.

Although the market is bullish, psychological resistance at 6.5 percent for the 30-year bond yield is unlikely to be breached until next week's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan is out of the way, traders said.
Greenspan will testify before a House Banking subcommittee next Tuesday. On the following day, he will also testify before the Senate Banking Committee.

"In addition to Greenspan testimony, we have corporate bond supplies and two- and five-year note offerings next week. The long bond may just hover at around 6.5 percent for the time being," said a trader at a Japanese brokerage house.
The September T-bond futures contract stood at 114-00/32, up from 113-30/32 from the previous close. The contract moved in a range of 113-30 and 114-02.
